extracted.intended_audience: aspiring improvisers of all levels (beginners to experienced) seeking in-person improv training in Chicago
extracted.subtask_description: A multi-level in-person improv training program (Levels 1–5) teaching short- and long-form improvisation, ensemble skills, and The Harold, with specified class logistics, schedules, and progression/prerequisite guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Class logistics and format
rubrics_metrics.description: Classes meet once a week for three hours. There are 7 class meetings per level. The average class size is between 10-14 people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All classes include a ‘celebration’ show at the end of the term. Term dates and specific meeting days/times vary by section; see schedule. Click here for more information regarding our class policies and Registration FAQs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Level 1 learning objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Using fun and unique exercises, in this class you will be introduced to our style and approach to improv and “longform” improvisation, learn new ways to improve essential communication and cooperation skills, creativity, and confidence in a very fun and supportive environment that fosters creativity, provides growth, and invaluable tools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All Level 1 classes include a Graduation Show. (There are no prerequisites to begin at this level.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Level 2 learning objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Designed to help you discover your strengths as an improviser, this level will focus on character creation, object/environment work, and most importantly, working as an ensemble and building a “group mind”.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After completing this level you will have learned essential listening skills, team-focused collaboration skills, and exceptional support skills to help make you a more confident, supportive, and reliable player in any type of improvisational performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Level 3 learning objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: The HOME Theater’s unique Charcuterie Board of Scenework Instruction. Our Level 3 curriculum puts emphasis on our approach to long-form improvisation and is designed to offer students insight, advice, and notes on long-form scene-work from a variety of veteran instructors and performers in a single 7-week term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: *Read Additional Info section below for pre-requisites on skipping levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Level 4 learning objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Building on the foundation of the first 3 levels, Level 4 will teach you “The Harold,” the Chicago-born signature long-form structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The techniques and skills you learn from The Harold will prepare you for any other longform style you’ll ever encounter. *Read Additional Info section below for pre-requisites on skipping levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Level 5 learning objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: This is the advanced Harold level, where you will heavily explore this long-form signature piece, learn what the Harold is really all about, and work toward mastering it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (This class will culminate in a performance.) *Read Additional Info section below for pre-requisites on skipping levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Harold (definition and importance)
rubrics_metrics.description: In the vast landscape of improv, the “Harold” format reigns as a shining star, earning its stripes as one of the most innovative improv comedy performance pieces known around the world.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This signature ‘long-form’ structure was created and perfected by the legendary Del Close and Charna Halpern right here in Chicago, whose work helped to make America’s “second city” the cool kid on the improv block.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensemble / group-mind and support skills
rubrics_metrics.description: Core emphasis across levels on working as an ensemble and building a “group mind”; developing essential listening skills, team-focused collaboration skills, and exceptional support skills.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Philosophy: nothing builds ensemble like going through the trenches together; students are encouraged to progress through levels with the same cohort to foster ensemble growth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character, object, and environment work
rubrics_metrics.description: Level 2 emphasis on character creation, object/environment work as fundamental scenework tools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These skills are taught to help students discover strengths as improvisers and contribute effectively to scenes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instructor experience and variety
rubrics_metrics.description: Led and curated by some of the most influential instructors in the field of improvisation of the past 30+ years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Level 3 explicitly offers notes and instruction on long-form scene-work from a variety of veteran instructors and performers — implying diversity of instructors and perspectives is a program feature and evaluative quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prerequisite / skipping-level policy
rubrics_metrics.description: If your improv experience consists of having taken more than one level of improv classes from an improv theater (iO, CIC, UCB, etc.), exceptions could be made where you will be allowed to register for any level you think you will be comfortable in, given your prior experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Despite exceptions, the theater highly encourages all new students to start at level 1 because of their progressive training approach and belief that ensemble-building benefits from shared progression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tuition pricing and term information
rubrics_metrics.description: LEVEL 1 SPECIAL CLASS PRICES: MONDAY – THURSDAY EVENING CLASSES: $225 – WEEKEND AND WEEKDAY CLASSES: $175. Levels 2–5 listed at $225.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Term 4, 2026 runs the week of June 15th through the week of August 3rd. (No Classes June 29th to July 5th). Specific meeting dates/times for each section are provided with each class listing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance outcomes / culminating shows
rubrics_metrics.description: All classes include a ‘celebration’ show at the end of the term; Level 1 classes include a Graduation Show; Level 5 culminates in a performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These in-term shows serve both as practice/performance assessment opportunities and as stated course outcomes.
